validation_scope.alternate_simulator_compatibility: Not established. A successful ngspice run must be labeled ngspice and must not be described as a PSpice run.

models.target_simulator: PSpice product-page model; header gives no simulator version
manufacturer_declared_features: Aol and phase with load effects
input voltage and current noise spectra
settling and overshoot versus capacitive load
input common-mode range and offset dependence
limitations_and_review_notes: The declared features do not explicitly validate controlled supply-startup behavior, chopper ripple, aliasing, or every off-state/back-power condition.
The header records convergence changes for single/asymmetric supplies. Preserve the latest model before evaluating the actual positive/negative rail ramps.
Noise-bearing device models require the simulator's noise analysis; an ordinary deterministic transient waveform is not a measurement of random voltage noise.

common_mode_table.interpretation: Specified electrical-characteristics range endpoints, not solely typical headroom values from the product-page selector.

offset_table.limitation: The macro-model's deterministic offset and drift are not the datasheet worst-case envelope.

datasheet_review.full_temperature_support: The adjacent CMRR rows specify minimum CMRR over -40 to +125 degC using this common-mode range at both +/-18V and +/-2.25V supplies.
startup_review: Section 8.3.6, printed pages 24-25, describes ESD steering-diode paths: inputs exceeding supply rails can inject current into the supplies. An input applied before a supply is established can back-power the amplifier or produce large current if that supply is low impedance; this is not normal operation.
The datasheet directs limiting input current to 10mA when the steering-diode path conducts. Consider actual supply sink capability and source/input resistance for power sequencing.

The description mentions controlled startup, but no quantitative supply-startup-to-final-offset settling specification was found. Normal signal-step settling figures must not be substituted for a precision startup guarantee.

Section 8.3.3 describes input-switch charge injection and recommends RC filtering to reduce output effects; the macro-model's ordinary noise/settling analyses do not establish all chopper-clock feedthrough or aliasing behavior.

models.vendor_distribution_format: TINA-TI Spice model; not the PSpice model package
manufacturer_declared_features: Aol and phase with load effects
input voltage and current noise spectra
settling and overshoot versus capacitive load
input common-mode range and offset dependence
limitations_and_review_notes: The generic non-Q1 model is preserved using its original file and subcircuit names; no rename, edit, or artificial conversion was performed.
The ZIP includes OPAx320.TLD and OPAx320.TSM as TINA collateral; the complete original ZIP preserves them. Only OPAx320.LIB was extracted.
The header names OPA320 and OPA2320 as the single and dual variants. This avoids silently relying on the Q1 model currently linked by the PSpice package.
No simulator was run by this research task. If the unmodified model runs in ngspice, that is ngspice validation of a TI TINA-distributed macro-model, not a PSpice result.
Noise and supply-startup model limitations remain applicable; validate quantitative fidelity against the intended device and test conditions.

manufacturer_declared_features: output voltage, initial accuracy, and temperature coefficient
quiescent current versus temperature and voltage
supply-flow output current and output-current limit
total output voltage noise from 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz
limitations_and_review_notes: The unmodified 2011 model selects its internally named A GRADE group. Its STANDARD GRADE option requires the documented mutually exclusive four-line group change; no such change was made. Do not infer current ordering-suffix equivalence from that model label alone.
The model header limits functional temperature use to -55 through +125 degC and warns that some parameters do not follow the physical device over that range.
The header states that PSRR matches DC and low-frequency behavior but does not match the datasheet at high frequencies. It cannot establish rejection of the 250-kHz charge-pump ripple.

The documented noise feature is total 0.1-to-10-Hz output noise; accuracy over a wider integration band must be checked against the intended device's datasheet. Peak-to-peak low-frequency specifications are not integrated RMS noise.

Startup and startup settling are explicitly represented, but the header supplies no universal startup tolerance or validation range for arbitrary input slew, trim/output capacitance, load, or externally driven output. Use actual circuit conditions and report model behavior separately from guaranteed hardware behavior.

The current datasheet's 200-us turn-on value is typical, at CL=1uF, to 0.1%; it is not a maximum settling guarantee for an externally filtered offset network. A TRIM/NR capacitor lengthens startup; 1uF produces about a 10-to-20-Hz noise filter.
The netlist contains a diode flicker-noise model (DVN, KF=1.05E-16); ordinary transient analysis alone does not demonstrate its random-noise spectrum.
This old model does not characterize the newer REF5025EI enhanced-grade option.

A compact behavioral LDO macro implements reference ramping, enable/UVLO, approximate line coupling, output resistance, dropout, and current limit. These are netlist observations, not independently validated silicon fidelity.
The model has no explicit device output-noise generator or noise-reduction pin. Its incidental resistor noise must not be equated to the physical LDO's specified integrated output noise.

The model predates the 2026 TPS723 Rev.E datasheet's new/legacy chip distinction and uses 280-mV dropout. Do not silently substitute the new chip's 140-mV typical dropout or claim new-chip startup/noise validation.
The official encrypted reference-project alternative is https://www.ti.com/lit/zip/SLVM866; it was inspected in memory but is not duplicated here.
